items.stem:
The diagram shows two towns A and B.
B is 9.6 km from A and the bearing of B from A is 052°.

parts.t: Calculate how far B is north of A.
Calculate how far B is east of A.
Write down the bearing of A from B.

sols: The bearing 052° is measured clockwise from north, so the 52° angle is between the north line and AB.
The distance north is the side adjacent to the 52° angle in the right-angled triangle.
The distance east is the side opposite the 52° angle.
The two north lines at A and at B are parallel, so the back bearing is 180° more.

The diagram shows triangle PQR.
PQ = 7.3 cm, QR = 11.6 cm and PR = 12.4 cm.
sols: All three sides are known and an angle is wanted, so use the cosine rule with the side PR = 12.4 cm opposite angle PQR.
rearrange to make cos PQR the subject
the cosine is positive, so the angle is acute — as the diagram suggests
ms:
M2 for cos PQR = (7.3² + 11.6² − 12.4²)⁄(2 × 7.3 × 11.6) oe
(M1 for 12.4² = 7.3² + 11.6² − 2 × 7.3 × 11.6 cos PQR oe)
M1 for cos PQR = 0.2012… or 34.09⁄169.36

items.stem:
The diagram shows a pyramid with a square base ABCD of side 10 cm.
The vertex V is vertically above the centre O of the base and VA = VB = VC = VD = 13 cm.

parts.t: Calculate the height VO of the pyramid.
Calculate the angle between the edge VA and the base ABCD.
Calculate the angle between the face VBC and the base ABCD.

sols: Pythagoras' theorem in the square base
the diagonals of a square bisect each other
AO is the projection of AV on the base, so the required angle is angle VAO.
Let M be the midpoint of BC. Then VM ⊥ BC and OM ⊥ BC, so the angle between the face and the base is angle VMO.
the line of intersection of the two planes is BC
O is the centre of the square
ms:
M1 for tan = their 10.9⁄7.07… or cos = 7.07…⁄13
A1
FT their (a)
